paper_title: Shifting Long-Context LLMs Research from Input to Output
caption: Proportion of real-user demand: The aforementioned 2K range refers to the interval [2K, 4K), and similarly for the other ranges. Solid color fill for input demand, slash fill for output demand in the Wildchat dataset.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the proportion of real-user demand for different input and output token length ranges in the Wildchat dataset, categorized into 2K, 4K, 8K, and 16K intervals (where, for example, 2K refers to the range [2K, 4K)). The vertical axis represents the "Number" of requests, scaled linearly from 0 to 120,000. The horizontal axis displays four groups, each corresponding to a token length range, with two bars per group: one for input demand (solid color fill) and one for output demand (slash fill). For the 2K range, the input demand (solid yellow) is 9,320, while the output demand (yellow with slashes) is 78,188. In the 4K range, input demand (solid orange) is 3,784 and output demand (orange with slashes) is 108,494. For the 8K range, input demand (solid blue) is 1,401 and output demand (blue with slashes) is 17,865. In the 16K range, input demand (solid dark blue) is 832 and output demand (dark blue with slashes) is 4,247. The bars are arranged in groups by token range, with input bars on the left and output bars on the right within each group. The chart clearly shows that output demand significantly exceeds input demand across all ranges, with the 4K output demand being the highest at 108,494. The legend at the bottom identifies the color and fill pattern for each category.
